title: model catalog: add filters, compatibility flags, and pricing/limits to capability endpoints (streaming & structured output + OpenAI compat)
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: expose richer model-catalog capability metadata and server-side filters for the public capability endpoints so clients and the OpenAI-compat layer can discover models by streaming support, tool/function-calling, structured-output schemas, and explicit pricing/limits. This PR adds new query filters to /v1/models and /v1/capabilities, surface flags on model objects, pricing fields for per-token costs and concurrency/limit metadata, and compatibility helpers for the OpenAI-compatibility layer. Key user stories: 1) SDKs can list only models that support streaming and function-calling, 2) the console can surface cost per token and max_token limits for vendor selection, 3) the OpenAI-compat gateway can select the best model variant at routing time. High-level changes: updated endpoint handlers to accept query params like supports_streaming, supports_tool_calling, supports_structured_output, openai_compatible, min_quality_score; extended model catalog schema with flat fields: "supports_streaming", "supports_tool_calling", "structured_output_schema_id", "openai_compatible", "pricing_input_token_price", "pricing_output_token_price", "max_total_tokens", "max_concurrency", "regional_limits" (strings for limits). Added server-side indexing to keep query latency under 10ms for common filters and small optimizations to the cache invalidation path when model metadata changes. Compatibility: existing clients see no breaking changes; new fields are opt-in and filtering defaults to not restricting results unless query params are provided. The OpenAI-compat layer now maps openai-compatible models to their equivalent model name and prioritizes models with matching pricing/limits when selecting a fallback. Streaming stability work: standardized SSE chunk delimiter, added keepalive pings and graceful pause/resume semantics for chunked responses to better support slow clients. Structured output: models can surface a schema_id and the endpoint now returns a short schema reference and validation hints to help SDKs and Console render structured result previews. Rollout plan: feature-flagged server-side rollout for 72 hours, smoke tests across hosted and dedicated clusters, SDK minor-version bumps to pick up filter helpers. Testing: unit tests for API handlers, integration tests against redwood-sdk-python and redwood-sdk-typescript, e2e streaming tests, and compatibility tests for OpenAI flow. Checklist: [x] API design doc linked in Linear ENG-4821, [x] unit/integration tests, [x] perf benchmark within SLA, [x] docs snippets for SDKs, [x] migration notes for Console. No breaking changes expected.

release_notes: Added capability filters to model listing endpoints: supports_streaming, supports_tool_calling, supports_structured_output, openai_compatible. Models now include pricing fields (pricing_input_token_price, pricing_output_token_price), operational limits (max_total_tokens, max_concurrency) and a structured_output_schema_id for result validation. OpenAI compatibility layer updated to prioritize pricing/latency-aware fallbacks. Streaming stability improved with keepalive pings and pause/resume semantics. No breaking changes. SDKs updated with helper filters.
summary: Expose capability filters and pricing/limits on model catalog endpoints, improve streaming stability and OpenAI compatibility routing; merged to main behind feature flag and covered by unit/integration/e2e tests
